put.summary: Changes a user's role or blocked status.
put.description:
Administrator-only endpoint. The API prevents an administrator from blocking or demoting
themselves to avoid losing the last admin session accidentally.

post.summary: Logs in with a Google Identity Services ID token.
post.description:
Use this endpoint in production login flows. The frontend sends the Google ID token from
Google Sign-In, and the API returns an encrypted JWE access token plus an opaque refresh token.

post.summary: Logs in as a seeded user for local development.
post.description:
Development-only endpoint for testing protected APIs before a Google frontend exists.
Use seeded emails such as admin@example.com. This endpoint returns 404 outside Development.

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token and refresh token. The old refresh
token is rotated and should be discarded by the client.
Revokes the authenticated session represented by the Bearer access token.

Creates the bill header only. Add members and calculate splits before publishing.
The authenticated user becomes the bill owner.

get.summary: Lists bills for the authenticated user.
get.description:
By default returns bills owned by the current user. Set owed=true to list bills where
the current user is one of the members who owes money.

put.description: Only the bill owner can update a bill, and only while it is still in Draft status.

get.summary: Gets a bill with split and payment status.
get.description: The current user must be the bill owner or one of the bill members.

post.summary: Adds members to a draft bill.
post.description:
The bill owner can add members by email, by group member ID, or include themselves.
Splits should be recalculated after changing members.

delete.summary: Removes a member from a draft bill.
delete.description: Only the bill owner can remove members. Removing a member requires recalculating splits.

post.summary: Calculates split amounts for a draft bill.
post.description:
Use Equal to split the total evenly across bill members, or Custom to submit exact member amounts.
The sum of custom allocations must equal the bill total.

put.summary: Configures the bank account that will receive VietQR payments for this bill.
put.description:
Only the bill owner can configure it, and only while the bill is Draft.
Each member will receive a VietQR containing their own remaining split amount.

post.summary: Publishes a bill and starts payment tracking.
post.description:
Only the bill owner can publish. The bill must have members and calculated split amounts
whose total equals the bill total.

Only the bill owner can cancel. Bills with recorded payments cannot be cancelled through
this endpoint because they need adjustment or refund handling.

Only the bill owner can request reminders. Submit memberIds to target specific members,
or omit memberIds to remind all members with outstanding amounts.

post.summary: Records a manual payment for a bill member.
post.description:
The bill owner confirms that a member paid outside the system, for example by cash or bank transfer.
The amount cannot exceed the member's outstanding split amount.

post.summary: Creates a group for splitting bills with recurring members.
post.description:
The authenticated user becomes the group owner. Use groups for shared contexts such as
family subscriptions, trips or house expenses.

get.summary: Lists groups visible to the authenticated user.
get.description: Returns groups where the current user is owner or active member. Results are paginated.

get.summary: Gets group details, members and related bills.
get.description: The current user must belong to the group. Owners also receive ownership flags used by the UI.

post.summary: Adds members to a group by email.
post.description:
Only the group owner can add members. Existing users are linked immediately; unknown emails
are created as pending members and can activate later through Google login.

delete.summary: Removes a member from a group.
delete.description:
Only the group owner can remove active members. The relationship is marked removed instead
of hard-deleted so history can remain auditable.

post.description: Only the owner can close a group. Closed groups cannot receive new members or be used for new bills.
